analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is an undersized destination buffer passed to wolfSSL radix-conversion APIs. baseConversion() calls mp_radix_size(mp, base, &size), allocates exactly size bytes, and then calls mp_toradix(mp, str, base). In this SP-MATH build, base can be invalid (e.g. not 10 or 16 for sp_toradix), and size computation does not guarantee enough space for the actual write path used by sp_tohex/sp_toradix, leading to a 1-byte heap overflow when sp_tohex writes the terminator/content past the allocation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: From the harness, fuzz input controls Bignum::GetPtr()->baseConversion() via the optional convert flag and chosen base byte. When convert is enabled and a crafted/unsupported base value is used, baseConversion still allocates based on mp_radix_size and unconditionally calls mp_toradix. Under WOLFSSL_SP_MATH_ALL this reaches sp_toradix/sp_tohex with a too-small heap buffer (seen as 1-byte allocation in ASan trace), causing an out-of-bounds write.
